title: Love appointed
hookLine: the Merciful will appoint love for those who believe and do good (19:96)
last: YA ABATI — PEACE BE UPON YOU.

lines: NOT THE LOUDEST IN THE ROOM.
cards: Some people are like this: not the loudest at the party, not the most well-known, not the one working hardest to be liked. And yet when their name comes up, faces soften. Neighbors bring them soup when they're sick.
Their funeral, when it comes, is full. Nobody can quite say how it happened. Near the end of Surah Maryam, a verse names what happened, and who did it.

teach.b: Verse ninety-six, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love."
The Beneficent is ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful, a name of God that comes back again and again in Surah Maryam.

The word for love is wudd: warm, steady affection, the kind that lasts. It shares its root with one of God's names, al-Wadud, the Loving. And the verb is sa-yaj'alu: He will make, He will place, He will appoint.
Love here isn't earned like a wage or chased like a prize. It's placed, by God, in hearts. Whose hearts?
Some commentators said other people's, so the good are loved by those around them. Some said: between the believers themselves. Some said: God's own love for them.

The Arabic leaves room for all three. A hadith in Bukhari and Muslim draws the picture. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: when God loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says, I love this person, so love them.
Then Jibril calls out to the people of heaven: God loves this person, so love them. And the people of heaven love them. Then acceptance is placed for them on earth.
It starts in heaven and arrives on earth last; the neighbor bringing soup is the end of a long chain.

teach.h: BELIEVE AND DO GOOD. NOT: BE LIKED.
teach.b: And the verse asks people to believe and do good. It doesn't say: try to be liked. Surah Maryam opened with Zakariyya calling in secret, then Yahya's tenderness and Ibrahim's peace.

teach.h: THE BENEFICENT WILL APPOINT FOR THEM LOVE.
teach.b: It closes with love that is given, not grabbed.

how: Muslims cite 19:96 and the hadith of Jibril's call when speaking of the love people feel for the righteous; teachers emphasize doing good sincerely, for God, rather than to be admired.

o: a marriage arranged by the two families
love you earn by working to be liked
love that God places in hearts for the good

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: the Loving: a name of God
God loves this person, so love them

s: 19:96 tells believers to work at being liked
it asks for faith and good works; the love is placed by God.
in the hadith, love on earth comes first, then in heaven
it begins with God and Jibril, then the people of heaven, and arrives on earth last.
wudd shares a root with al-Wadud, a name of God

games.q: when God loves a servant, the hadith says, whom does He call first?
games.why: Jibril, then the people of heaven, and then acceptance is placed for that person on earth (Bukhari and Muslim).

practice: Choose one good thing you could do that no one will see or thank you for: taking out a neighbor's bins, paying for someone's coffee and leaving before they notice, or, if you pray, praying for someone who's unkind to you.
Picture doing it and walking away without telling anyone, and notice the small pull to be seen. Let it go, and leave the love, if it comes, for God to place.

wordCard.voice: Love appointed. Wudd, warm and lasting love, placed by the Most Merciful for those who believe and do good. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: love, warm affection (19:96); from the root of al-Wadud, the Loving.

carryVoice: Your line: love will be appointed. It starts in heaven, not in the crowd. Day four hundred seventy-four, done.

sources.q: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3209; Sahih Muslim 2637 (God calls Jibril)
